assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: a patient without this variant produces mostly equivocal CMAP amplitude

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.predicate: larger response at the elbow level
assertions.quote: the wrist response is smaller because of the median nerve axonal crossover, consequently leading to a larger response at the elbow level

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.predicate: difference between elbow and wrist less than or equal to 25%
assertions.quote: A difference of less than or equal to 25% between the elbow and wrist would be acceptable in patients with an MGA

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.predicate: difference between elbow and wrist larger than 25%
assertions.quote: A difference larger than 25% would raise suspicion for a true ulnar or median nerve neuropathy, respectively

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: F-waves and H-reflexes are not helpful when evaluating ulnar neuropathy due to nonspecificity

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: the most commonly tested hand muscles innervated by the ulnar nerve are the abductor digiti minimi (ADI) and the first dorsal interosseus (FDI)

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: If an axonal lesion is present, these muscles will likely be positive compared to the forearm muscles

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.predicate: high amplitude, delayed duration, fibrillation potentials, and positive sharp waves
assertions.quote: high amplitude, delayed duration, fibrillation potentials, and positive sharp waves may be seen in the intrinsic hand muscles innervated by the ulnar nerve and the FCU

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: Chronic and severe proximal or distal ulnar nerve axonal injury or entrapment can lead to delayed recruitment and monophasic waves

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
